title: 4 debugging moves seniors use
sources: git-scm.com/docs/git-bisect: binary search for the commit that introduced a bug
developer.chrome.com DevTools docs: logpoints (right-click line number > Add logpoint) and conditional breakpoints
The Pragmatic Programmer (Hunt & Thomas): rubber duck debugging

lines.text: Four debugging moves seniors use | that tutorials *never* show you.
First, *git bisect.* | Tell git one *good* commit and one *bad* one, | and it searches the history by halves | until it finds the commit that *broke* it.
Second, *logpoints* in Chrome DevTools. | Right-click a line number, | and it logs any value | *without* touching your code.
Third, *conditional breakpoints.* | The code only pauses when something you choose is *true,* | like the one bad item | in a list of *ten thousand.*
And finally, *rubber duck* debugging. | Explain your code out loud, line by line, | and the bug often shows up | *before* you finish.
Save this for the next time something *breaks.*
If you want skills like this, | a few minutes a day, | the link's in my *bio.* | It's called *Teyro.*
